title: A Left Loin Scar / One Kidney Gone: Protect the One Left

blocks.text: A Left Loin Scar / One Kidney Gone: Protect the One Left

AMaC MRCP PACES · R2-11 · Physical examination · PACES Station 4, abdominal examination encounter · Skills A, B, D, E, G · 10 min: up to 6 min examining, then at least 4 min of examiner questions · Guidelines: NICE NG203 Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management (published 25 August 2021; last updated 24 November 2021) · Related AMaC: Abdominal examination: renal transplant; polycystic kidneys
Mr Vikram Sethi, 59, an accountant, attends for a routine check. Please examine his abdomen and report what you find. You have up to 6 minutes to examine, followed by questions.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text: The Hook. An oblique loin scar suggests previous renal surgery; confirm whether it was nephrectomy; the lesson is why it was done and how to protect the single kidney that remains.

The Examiner Trap. Candidates see the scar, say "nephrectomy" and stop, never giving the reasons or the follow-up. Pass: name the scar, give the causes, and plan kidney protection. Fail: stop at the scar with no reasons and no plan.

rows: Look at the scar and the whole patient.
"Mr Sethi, may I examine your tummy and your side? Tell me if anything is sore."
Introduce, consent, ask about pain, expose; inspect the loin scar, abdomen, hands, ankles.
Is the remaining kidney normal, and is there a mass?
"I'm going to feel your tummy and both sides."
Palpate; ballot kidneys; scar for incisional hernia; liver and spleen; ascites.
Look for effects on the remaining kidney.
"I'd like to take your blood pressure and test your urine."
Give reasons for the nephrectomy and the follow-up.
"This is a left nephrectomy. I'd ask why, then check kidney function and urine protein."
Cover him, thank him; present findings, causes, plan.
Presses on the scar without asking; leaves him exposed
Introduces, obtains consent, cleans hands, asks about pain, covers him
Offers a chaperone, asks about scar tenderness and thanks him
No inspection of the scar; no ballotting
Inspects scar, palpates, ballots the right kidney, checks for hernia
Compares both renal angles and checks blood pressure and urine
Reports a palpable mass or hepatomegaly that is absent
Healed oblique left loin scar; no palpable left renal mass; right kidney not palpable
States no hernia, no mass, no oedema, BP 152/90 and urine protein
Left nephrectomy with a single kidney
Nephrectomy, with causes: cancer, donation, stones or infection, trauma
Says how to find the cause: ask the patient, then read his records
Kidney function, urine albumin:creatinine ratio, blood pressure
Classifies by GFR and urine ratio, and sets monitoring with him
Critical fail (AMaC practice flag, not an official automatic PACES fail): advises regular anti-inflammatory painkillers
Controls blood pressure, protects the kidney, takes care with anti-inflammatories
Adds surveillance if the cause was cancer, and treatment of blood pressure per NICE targets

blocks.text: High-performance is an AMaC teaching label, not an official grade. High-performance includes the pass behaviours. This station-specific grid is an AMaC teaching framework mapped to PACES skills, not an official mark scheme. Consent, hand hygiene, dignity and an appropriate chaperone are baseline professional practice. Critical fail is an AMaC practice flag for an action that could harm the patient today; it is not an official automatic PACES fail.
Not used for this station type: the patient is a real or simulated patient and the findings are in section 8.

Findings (released as each step is done). Healed oblique scar in the left loin; non-tender; no incisional hernia. No palpable left renal mass. Right kidney not ballotable. No masses; liver and spleen not palpable; no ascites. BP 152/90, pulse 76 (scenario values). No oedema. Urine dipstick protein 1+. Hands normal.

Question ladder. Q1 Findings and diagnosis (R3, R4): left nephrectomy. Q2 Causes (R5): renal cancer, living donation, stones with infection, trauma, polycystic disease. Q3 Investigations (R6): eGFR, urine albumin:creatinine ratio, blood pressure, classification by GFR and ratio (NICE NG203). Q4 Management (R7): treat hypertension, caution with long-term anti-inflammatories, surveillance if cancer.
Normal-findings variant for a separate teaching exercise. No scar, normal kidneys. The candidate must say the abdomen is normal. Do not switch the defined case to this variant during the encounter.
Curveball 1. "He takes ibuprofen daily for back pain." Safe: be cautious over long-term use; review alternatives.
Curveball 2. "Does he have chronic kidney disease?" Safe: not by the scar alone; check eGFR and urine ratio.
Curveball 3. "He donated a kidney." Safe: donors are followed; check blood pressure and kidney tests.
Introduces, consents and asks about pain (G)
Inspects the scar and describes it (A)
Ballots both kidneys and compares the renal angles (A)
Checks for incisional hernia (A)
Reports the scar, no palpable left renal mass and no mass (B)
Names left nephrectomy (D)
Gives causes of nephrectomy (D)
Requests eGFR and urine albumin:creatinine ratio (E)
Takes blood pressure and tests urine (E)
Advises caution with anti-inflammatories (E)
Covers and thanks him (G)
Fail performance
(Presses on the scar without asking. [R1 Fail] Does not ballot the kidneys. [R2 Fail])
CANDIDATE: There is a mass in the left loin. [R3 Fail] This is a renal transplant. [R4 Fail] I can't say why. [R5 Fail]
EXAMINER: What would you do?
CANDIDATE: A CT scan. [R6 Fail] He can take ibuprofen for pain. [R7 Fail]

Examiner note: No pain check, an invented mass, wrong diagnosis and a Critical fail (AMaC practice flag, not an official automatic PACES fail): advising regular anti-inflammatories for a single kidney.
Pass performance
CANDIDATE: (Cleans hands.) Hello Mr Sethi, I'm one of the doctors. May I examine your tummy and side? Is it sore anywhere? Tell me if anything hurts. [R1 Pass]
(Inspects the scar, palpates, ballots the right kidney and checks for hernia. [R2 Pass])
CANDIDATE: There is a healed oblique left loin scar, no palpable left renal mass and no right kidney mass. [R3 Pass]
CANDIDATE: This is a probable previous left nephrectomy, to confirm from history and imaging. [R4 Pass] Causes include cancer, donation and stones with infection. [R5 Pass]
CANDIDATE: Thank you, Mr Sethi. I'll cover you. [R1 Pass]
EXAMINER: What would you check?
CANDIDATE: Kidney function, the urine albumin:creatinine ratio and blood pressure. [R6 Pass]
EXAMINER: And advice?
CANDIDATE: Control his blood pressure, protect the kidney, and be careful with anti-inflammatories. [R7 Pass]
Examiner note: Safe and accurate. Did not classify or ask for his records.
High-performance performance
CANDIDATE: (Cleans hands.) Hello Mr Sethi, I'm one of the doctors. May I examine your tummy and side? Is it sore anywhere? Tell me if anything hurts. [R1 High]
(Inspects the scar, palpates, ballots the right kidney and checks for hernia. [R2 High])
CANDIDATE: May I offer a chaperone? Is the scar tender? Tell me if I press too hard. [R1 High]
(Compares both renal angles, checks blood pressure and tests urine. [R2 High])
CANDIDATE: A healed left loin scar, no hernia or mass, no oedema; BP 152/90 and protein 1+ on dipstick. [R3 High]
CANDIDATE: A left nephrectomy for cancer, donation, stones or infection, or trauma. [R4 High]
CANDIDATE: I'd ask him why, then read his records. [R5 High]
EXAMINER: What would you check?
CANDIDATE: eGFR and the urine ratio, then classify the kidney disease and agree monitoring with him. [R6 High]
EXAMINER: And advice?
CANDIDATE: Treat blood pressure to the NICE target; caution with anti-inflammatories; surveillance if it was for cancer. [R7 High]
CANDIDATE: Thank you for letting me examine you. [R1 High]
Examiner note: Found the cause by asking, classified the risk and tailored the advice.
R7: Advising regular anti-inflammatory painkillers for a man with one kidney risks further kidney damage.
R2: Not inspecting the scar or comparing the renal angles misses the key sign.
R3: Reporting a loin mass that is absent suggests signs were assumed.
R4: Calling it a transplant ignores the oblique loin scar and the no palpable left renal mass.
R5: Naming no cause leaves the diagnosis unexplained.
"Let me compare both sides of the loin."
"I'd ask him why it was removed."
"I'd protect the remaining kidney."
Nephrectomy scar: oblique loin or midline incision; non-palpability does not confirm an absent kidney; the other kidney may be enlarged.

NICE NG203 (published 25 August 2021; last updated 24 November 2021): classify CKD using GFR and ACR; exercise caution giving anti-inflammatories over prolonged periods; aim clinic systolic below 140 mmHg when ACR is under 70 mg/mmol.
A single kidney alone is not CKD: check eGFR and ACR.

A loin scar can follow several renal operations; neither kidney being palpable does not prove nephrectomy. Confirm anatomy and indication from history and records. Quantify proteinuria with ACR and check persistence before assigning CKD. Use CKD BP targets only if CKD is established and individualise for frailty and treatment tolerance.
THINK: Protect the single kidney.
SAY: "A probable previous left nephrectomy, to confirm from history and imaging."
DO: Scar; ballot both sides; BP and urine.
NUMBERS: BP 152/90; systolic below 140 mmHg if ACR under 70 mg/mmol (NICE NG203).
TRAP: Stopping at the scar.
FINISH: eGFR and ACR; BP control; caution with anti-inflammatories.

NICE NG203 Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management (published 25 August 2021; last updated 24 November 2021). CKD classification; ACR; NSAIDs; clinic BP targets 1.6.1 and 1.6.2. https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng203/chapter/Recommendations.
